rail_guard.text: All aboard the heritage line! Steam, whistles and a cup of tea on the platform.

then.text: Red and white, under the hill. The red one won. The white one went to England. Mostly.
That's the version my nain told. The English version has a more complicated plot and a longer tea break.

else.text: Ah, a listener. Good. Sit, or at least stop leaning on the harp. Croeso.
Long ago, King Vortigern wanted a fortress on a hill called Dinas Emrys. Every night, the walls fell down.
A boy named Emrys, who we call Myrddin, told him why. Under the hill, there's a pool. And in the pool, two dragons, asleep.
One red, one white. They fought, as dragons will, over who got the better ground floor. The red one won.
The red dragon is Y Ddraig Goch. She is on the flag. She is on a lot of pubs.
She went back to sleep, under the mountain. But they say that if the stones ever hum together, she'll hear it.
I'd let sleeping dragons lie, myself. But I'm a harpist. We're not very good at telling people no.

then.text: Rain! The tenors love it. It gives them something to grumble about between verses.
Choir practice at dusk. You'll hear us across the Dee. The sheep have started joining in.

choir_boss.text: Llangollen's International Musical Eisteddfod started in 1947, to heal the world with songs.
Fifty-odd countries turn up. We warm up by arguing over the sheet music. Perfect harmony.

then.text: Raining up in the Berwyns, so the Dee will be up by teatime. Mind your boots, cariad.
Mist on the river this morning. The old bridge looks like it's floating.

bridge_keeper.text: That's the Chain Bridge, out at Berwyn. Walkers only, mind. Cars use the old stone bridge in town.
The Dee floods and the town puts the bridge back. We're a patient lot.

castle_climber.text: Castell Dinas Brân. Medieval castle on top of an Iron Age hillfort. The crows were first.
Three hundred-odd metres up. Sixty seconds of views per hundred of puff.

then.text: Fog and steam together. You can't tell where the train ends and the weather begins. Glorious.
Sun's out, the engine's polished, and the whistle's going. Best day of the year, this.

steam_fan.text: The Llangollen Railway runs steam trains along the Dee. Proper ones, with whistles.
I don't ride. I just stand here and smell the coal. Bliss.

ladies_tour.text: Plas Newydd, up the hill, was home to the Ladies of Llangollen. Two friends, 1780s, famous for good taste.
Wordsworth and the Duke of Wellington dropped in for tea. They gave very high marks.

then.text: Sun's out! The horse-drawn boats are running on the canal. I'm waving at all of them.
Mam says I have to go in at dusk. Hwyl fawr! See? I told you I use it a lot.

canal_kid.text: Pob lwc, that's good luck. Lots of it needed when the harpist tunes up.
Hwyl fawr, that's goodbye. I use it a lot at bedtime.
